all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] shellTag matches only a shell name or a script ending .sh/.bash/.zsh/.dash/.ash/.ksh, so a shell's missing-command/EACCES line for an extension-less script ('./scripts/verify: line 3: pytest: command not found') matches no anchored shape. With a success signal present the evidence reads exit 0, so a run that died on a missing command is accepted; extension-less scripts are deferred to a receipt.

[ADVISORY] modalVerb keeps the mr-r3y set plus 'not' but omits can't/shouldn't/mustn't/isn't, so prose like 'the retry can't fail' is not neutralized. Such passing prose is read as a failure (fail-closed false positive); the contractions were left out to limit scope beyond mr-b08.

[ADVISORY] The shellTag comment omits the optional path prefix '(?:[^\s:]*/)?' the regex accepts, so '/bin/sh: ...' looks unsupported. A maintainer editing/auditing the shell shapes trusts the comment and misjudges what the pattern accepts.

[ADVISORY] The mr-b08 shape list omits the zsh reversed 'no such file or directory: <path>' form the code implements and a test covers. A reader of the doc misjudges that shape's coverage.

[ADVISORY] Several 'prose bare' negatives ('command not found handling is covered', 'permission denied is handled by the sandbox', the colon-tag case) lack the shell tag their target shapes require, so they do not isolate the line-start anchor they are grouped under. A regression dropping the shell-tag/anchor requirement would not be caught by those cases.
